extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals (PRSA members and communicators)
extracted.subtask_description: The PRSA Code of Ethics: a set of core values, provisions and interpretive guidelines that govern ethical practice for public relations professionals and guide the creation and distribution of communications (including press releases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve as responsible advocates for those we represent; act to advance the public interest by responsibly representing clients, employers and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for clients' legitimate interests while recognizing obligations to serve the public interest; present clients' views vigorously but honestly; avoid misrepresentation when promoting a position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure factual accuracy in all statements, releases and representations; avoid deceptive practices, fabrication, misrepresentation or omission of material facts; promptly correct errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience; continue professional development and provide informed counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain competence through education and training; rely on professional standards and evidence-based methods when planning and issuing communications; share expertise ethically with colleagues and clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide objective counsel, maintain intellectual independence and avoid unacceptable outside influences that would impair professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose and manage influences (client, sponsor, personal) that could impair objectivity; refuse assignments that require unethical conduct; preserve editorial and professional independence when preparing releases and other materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be faithful to those we represent while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance client or employer loyalty with responsibility to the public; avoid actions that disserve either the client or public trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness (core value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media and the public; respect all opinions and support open, honest and civil exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exploit privileged relationships to the unfair advantage of a client; treat competitors and media professionally and without sabotage; do not deliberately obstruct the information needs of the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect and advance the free flow of accurate and truthful information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote openness and transparency; do not use deceptive techniques to influence coverage; provide accurate, timely information and correct inaccuracies; do not suppress unfavorable information that is in the public interest to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote healthy and fair competition among public relations professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid undermining competitors through dishonest tactics; do not engage in plagiarism of others’ work; do not use bribery, covert pay-for-play or dishonest practices to secure coverage; respect proprietary rights and avoid inducements that compromise fair competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be honest and accurate in all communications; make full, fair and timely disclosure of information when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify sponsors and clients when issuing communications (including sponsored content and advertorials); disclose material interests, financial arrangements, gifts or outside employment that could influence messaging; clearly label paid placements; reveal if content has been materially altered by a sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect confidential and private information obtained in the course of professional work unless authorized or legally required to disclose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between information that is public, private or privileged; do not disclose confidential client/employer information without consent; when legal obligation requires disclosure, seek to limit scope and notify client/employer when permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest and fully disclose unavoidable conflicts to affected parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and disclose conflicts early to clients or employers; do not accept assignments or gifts that would impair impartiality or create appearance of impropriety; recuse yourself where necessary and avoid representing conflicting interests unless all parties are informed and consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold and advance the profession by mentoring, education, and increasing the public’s understanding of public relations practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support ethical behavior among colleagues; participate in professional development; contribute to research and public understanding; refrain from conduct that would bring discredit to the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, Attribution and Source Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure facts, statistics, quotes and sources in communications are accurate, verifiable and properly attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify claims before publication; identify sources accurately; do not fabricate quotes or attribute statements to fabricated or unwilling sources; correct misattributions and factual errors promptly and visibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Deceptive Practices (including online identity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not employ deceptive or covert techniques (e.g., fake identities, undisclosed paid endorsements) to persuade the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating or using false online personas to stir support; disclose the identity of communicators and sponsors; do not engage in stealth influence operations or undisclosed astroturfing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Paid or Sponsored Content / Native Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly and conspicuously disclose when content is paid for, sponsored or materially influenced by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label paid content, sponsored posts and advertorials in a way the intended audience can readily see and understand; avoid burying disclosures in terms and conditions or near unrelated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts, Gratuities and Inducements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept or offer gifts or gratuities that impair professional judgment or create appearance of impropriety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decline gifts that are intended to influence coverage or judgment; disclose modest hospitality where required by employer/client policy; avoid token payments to media for favorable coverage without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting Errors and Retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: When erroneous or misleading information has been published, correct it promptly and with appropriate prominence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue corrections or retractions with the same reach and visibility as the original dissemination; acknowledge responsibility when errors occur and explain corrective steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting Proprietary and Personal Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect proprietary, personal and trade-secret information obtained through client or employer relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement reasonable safeguards for records and data; do not disclose personal data or proprietary plans without authorization; comply with applicable privacy and data protection laws and client agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency About Representations and Relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose who you represent and any material relationships that bear on credibility of the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing an organization, individual or cause, identify that relationship in spokesperson roles and materials; disclose when you are compensated to influence opinion or when a third party produces material used in a release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Misuse of Media and Suppression of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not misuse media relationships (e.g., pay for placement without disclosure) or attempt to suppress information that should be available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect editorial independence; avoid contractual or other arrangements that would require suppressing unfavorable but true information that is in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for Content Distributed on Behalf of Others
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept accountability for content distributed on behalf of clients or employers; ensure content complies with ethical and legal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review third-party content incorporated into releases for accuracy and disclosure; require contractual provisions that permit you to refuse dissemination of unethical or illegal material.
